newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber closes steady on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber closes steady on shortcovering.

text.p: Rubber futures finished largely steady on Thursday on shortcovering, bucking a fall in Japanese prices, dealers said.
"There was some buying by European consumers this afternoon mainly for shortcovering reasons and this steadied the market despite the fall in Japanese prices," a local rubber trader said.
The buying was concentrated mainly in TSR20 and RSS3 rubber, the traders said.
Tokyo benchmark April contract fell 1.1 yen to settle at 142.9 while Kobe's April contract also dropped 1.1 yen to 143.0.
"The shortcovering allowed prices to hold or end just slightly lower this afternoon," a dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, December RSS3 was seen at 125.50-127.50 U.S. cents a kg compared with the previous 126.50 cents.
January RSS1 was seen at 183.00-185.00 Singapore cents (US$1.30-$1.32) a kg against 184.25 cents.
January TSR20 was seen at 178.00-180.00 Singapore cents (US$1.27-$1.28) a kg from 178.50 cents.
